title: kate-ui: name the session file and write it atomically
summary: session_path returns Library/Application Support/KateM5Rust/session.json under a home directory. write_text_atomically creates the parent directories, writes a sibling temp file, and renames it onto the path. The quit and launch packet uses both.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. The file has no GPUI import, but kate-ui tests run in the rust (macos-15) job and the Mac lane owns crates/kate-ui.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Add both functions with #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]. The temp file name is the file name plus .tmp plus the process id. On a write error remove the temp file and return the error. The test session_file_is_written_atomically makes a temp directory under std::env::temp_dir with the process id in its name, asserts session_path ends with KateM5Rust/session.json, writes {} to that path, reads it back, and removes the directory. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: profile::tests::session_file_is_written_atomically
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because session_path does not exist. After the change the path is under Library/Application Support/KateM5Rust and the text round-trips.
